glance: Fish restaurants near Boro Station, Chandpur
ilish-dim-bhuna.desc: Before spawning, female hilsa carry large sacs of roe, and in Chandpur these are treated as a delicacy in their own right. The roe is either fried until golden and crumbly or cooked with onion, chilli and turmeric into a rich bhuna. It is very filling and best eaten with plain rice and a squeeze of lime.

glance: One Minute sweet shop on Press Club Road, near Kalibari, Chandpur town
chandpur-one-minute-ice-cream.desc: Hilsa is the reason most people come to Chandpur, but the town also has a well-known ice cream of its own called One Minute. It is made in Chandpur and sold at the One Minute sweet shop on Press Club Road, close to Kalibari. Travel guides suggest it as the thing to have after an ilish lunch at Boro Station.

glance: Varies sharply by size and season; large fish cost far more per kg
Restaurants and stalls around Boro Station, Chandpur
chandpur-hilsa.desc: Hilsa swim up from the sea into the big rivers to spawn, and the waters around Chandpur are among the most famous places to catch them. Bangladeshis prize the local fish for its oily, delicate flesh and full flavour. Classic preparations include shorshe ilish, steamed in mustard paste, and simple fried slices served with the hot frying oil over rice. Riverside restaurants at Boro Station fry it fresh to order.

boro-station-fish-ghat.desc: Chandpur's main fish landing ghat is one of the busiest in the country. In season, boats arrive through the morning and their catch is laid out in silver heaps, then auctioned rapidly to traders who pack it in ice for Dhaka and beyond. The shouting, the smell of the river and the sheer quantity of fish make it a vivid slice of local life.
blocks: How to get there
At Boro Station, next to the Molehead.
Good to know
Go early in the morning. Watch your step on the wet floors, and stay out of porters' way.

chandpur-hilsa-fishing-life.desc: Thousands of families in Chandpur depend on hilsa fishing, setting out at night in wooden boats with long drift nets. Their year follows the fish: the Meghna near Chandpur is a hilsa sanctuary, and the government bans fishing there for part of the spring to protect young fish (jatka), with a further ban during the main autumn spawning period. Visiting the ghats or talking with boat crews gives a sense of how closely life here is tied to the river.
blocks: Good to know
Do not buy jatka (juvenile hilsa) or fish during ban periods; it harms the fishery and is illegal.

chandpur-meghna-char.desc: In the dry months, the falling Meghna reveals sandbars near Chandpur town, and one of them has become a casual outing spot that locals sometimes nickname 'mini Cox's Bazar'. A short boat ride takes you across to wide stretches of sand, with river on all sides and fishing boats drifting past. It is simple and unpolished, and best at sunset.
blocks: How to get there
Hire a trawler or engine boat from the Boro Station area; agree return times in advance.
Good to know
Go only in calm weather and in daylight, wear a life jacket and do not swim; Meghna currents are strong. The char's shape changes every year.

glance: 100 km to Chandpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
chandpur-molehead.desc: At the western edge of town, a stone-lined promontory called the Molehead juts into the water at Boro Station. From here you look across the place where the Dakatia joins the merging Padma and Meghna, a wide expanse that feels almost like the sea in the rainy season. The point has a Liberation War memorial nearby and is the town's favourite spot to watch the sunset. The currents are strong, so it is a place for looking, not swimming.
blocks: How to get there
Launches from Dhaka's Sadarghat reach Chandpur in about 3–4 hours; Boro Station is a short rickshaw ride from the launch terminal.
Good to know
Do not go into the water; this confluence is known for dangerous currents and whirlpools. Sunset is the best time.

glance: 100 km to Chandpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
rupsha-zamindar-bari.desc: The Rupsha zamindar family of Faridganj bought their estate roughly 250 years ago, and their descendants still live in the house today. A wide field opens in front of three brick buildings, and by the entrance stand the family graveyard and Masjid-e-Noor, a mosque founded in Bengali year 1284 (around 1877) by Mohammad Ghazi Chowdhury. The family is remembered locally for treating tenants well and for helping freedom fighters in 1971. It is an easy trip from Chandpur town and rarely crowded.
blocks: How to get there
From Chandpur town take a CNG or bus toward Faridganj and get off at Rupsha Bazar; the zamindar house is a short walk away.
Good to know
The family still lives here, so ask permission before going inside the compound or photographing the house.

glance: 100 km to Chandpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
lohagar-math.desc: Lohagar Math stands in Lohagar village of Faridganj upazila, beside the Dakatia river, and is said to be the only math in Chandpur district. Local tradition says it was built by the zamindar brothers Lohu and Gohor, after whom the village is named, and stories tell of a road paved with coins and a gold finial at the top. Its exact age is unknown; estimates range widely. Today the brick tower stands among village homes and trees, cracked but still striking.
blocks: How to get there
From Chandpur town take a CNG toward Faridganj and ask for Lohagar; it is close to the Dakatia bank.
Good to know
Do not climb the structure; it is old and fragile.

glance: 100 km to Chandpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
hajiganj-boro-mosque.desc: The Hajiganj Boro Mosque, built in the first half of the 20th century, is a landmark of Chandpur district. Its large prayer halls, decorated interiors and tall minaret draw worshippers from far around, particularly on Fridays and in Ramadan. It is a strong example of the region's religious architecture of that era.
blocks: How to get there
Hajiganj is about 30–40 minutes by bus or CNG east of Chandpur town on the Cumilla road.
Good to know
Dress modestly and avoid visiting at prayer times. Women should ask locally about access.
